title: When Should an Indian SaaS Business Move Away From a Merchant of Record?
summary: A Merchant of Record is a third party that acts as the legal seller to your end customer for the transactions covered by its agreement. An Indian SaaS
body_markdown:
A Merchant of Record is a third party that acts as the legal seller to your end customer for the transactions covered by its agreement. An Indian SaaS business should consider moving away when direct collection creates a clear commercial benefit and the team can manage the responsibilities it takes on. That means comparing total costs, checking buyer payment needs, assigning tax and export operations, and protecting subscription renewals.


Razorpay is worth evaluating when your Indian SaaS company wants to collect directly through eligible[international payments](https://razorpay.com/accept-international-payments/) , supported card subscriptions or invoice-led international bank transfers. Confirm the required products and account approvals before planning a migration. An MoR can still be the right choice when outsourced seller administration is more valuable than the potential savings or control. This guide helps you decide whether to stay, switch selected sales, or migrate more broadly.


### Key Takeaways


- Consider leaving an MoR when direct selling improves the full business case and your team can operate the responsibilities it takes back.
- Evaluate Razorpay for eligible direct international card collections, supported card subscriptions and invoice-led international bank transfers, according to how your buyers actually pay.
- Compare the MoR’s actual bundled contract with the full direct stack, including billing, tax operations, disputes, FX and migration costs.
- Direct collection leaves your SaaS business as seller. Assign owners for applicable tax, invoices, refunds, disputes and export records before switching.
- Check subscription and payment-method portability before promising a seamless move. Existing authorisations may need replacement.
- Staying with an MoR, or moving only a defined buyer segment, can be sensible when global administration or renewal risk outweighs the direct-selling benefit.


## What Must Be True Before an Indian SaaS Business Leaves an MoR?


An Indian SaaS business is ready to leave an MoR when it has a specific commercial reason, workable direct-collection economics, approved payment and billing flows, accountable tax and export operations, and a safe migration plan. If any of these remains unresolved, keep the affected sales on the existing arrangement while closing that gap.


### Use Readiness Checks Instead of a Universal Revenue Threshold


Independent analysis of MoR exits argues that outgrowing the model is driven by qualitative operating signals rather than a revenue milestone. Use these operational checks instead.


**Decision criterion** **Evidence that supports a switch** **Reason to wait or retain an MoR**


Commercial need


A documented constraint on contracts, invoices, checkout or billing is affecting your actual buyers


The current arrangement serves buyers well


All-in economics


Quotes and operating costs show a benefit after migration and retained responsibilities


The apparent saving disappears once equivalent services are included


Collection fit


Required currencies, cards, renewals or transfer rails are approved and tested


A material buyer segment would lose its preferred supported method


Operating readiness


Finance, advisers and engineering have explicit responsibilities and capacity


Nobody owns tax assessment, filings, disputes or export reconciliation


Migration feasibility


Consent, contracts, payment methods and renewals have a tested transition path


Authorisations or customer obligations cannot yet be moved safely


### Choose Whether to Stay, Move New Sales or Migrate Existing Subscribers


Three outcomes are legitimate. You can stay with the current MoR. You can route a clearly defined group of new buyers through direct collection while leaving existing renewals untouched. Or you can migrate eligible existing subscriptions after testing. A different MoR may also solve a provider-specific problem without changing the seller model. For the underlying model comparison, read the[merchant of record versus payment gateway](https://razorpay.com/blog/merchant-of-record-vs-payment-gateway-india/) guide. Creating an overseas entity is a separate legal decision, not a prerequisite for this one.


> **PRO-TIP:** Review a real renewal, a real enterprise invoice and one refund end to end before choosing an architecture. A product checklist alone will miss the handoffs between payments, billing and finance.


## When Does Razorpay Fit an Indian SaaS Business Moving to Direct Collection?


Razorpay is worth shortlisting when an eligible Indian SaaS business wants to remain the seller and collect directly from overseas customers. Evaluate international card checkout for self-serve purchases, supported card subscriptions for recurring plans, and International Bank Transfer for invoice-led collections. Confirm the required flow, currencies, business category and activation with Razorpay before switching.

Because the documented international-currency subscription flow relies on cards, do not assume domestic recurring rails such as UPI AutoPay or eMandates apply to foreign-currency plans.


### Where Razorpay Fits in a Direct SaaS Stack


If your SaaS team has arranged the tax and export operations that remain with the seller, Razorpay gives you payment collection options to assess against your customer journey. A self-serve subscription and an enterprise invoice may need different collection flows, with different activations and documentation. Choose Razorpay when the approved products support those flows and the complete cost and migration review supports the change. Keep an MoR for any segment where outsourced seller administration remains genuinely valuable.


One further architecture check matters for Indian exporters with large contracts. The RBI’s payment aggregator framework sets a per-transaction ceiling of Rs 25,00,000 for cross-border payment aggregator transactions. If an annual enterprise invoice could exceed that figure, confirm the appropriate collection route before moving that segment.


> **DID YOU KNOW:** A one-time international payment request and an international card subscription solve different collection tasks. Check the recurring-payment product and its authorisation requirements even if your business already accepts international one-time payments.


## What Responsibilities Stay With Your SaaS Business After Switching?


With direct collection, your SaaS company remains the seller and must arrange the tax, invoice, refund, dispute and export-record work applicable to its transactions. Razorpay supports the approved payment flow and related documentation. Confirm who does each remaining task before leaving an MoR, because payment acceptance alone does not transfer seller responsibilities.


### Assign Tax, Invoicing and Dispute Responsibilities


Responsibility

Do not equate tax calculation software with registration, filing and remittance.


Exposure varies by market:


-


**European Union:** A non-EU business can face EU VAT from its very first B2C digital-services sale, with no small-business registration threshold.


-


**United Kingdom:** A non-established business generally must register for UK VAT from its first taxable supply.


-


**United States:** SaaS is taxable in some form across 21 US states and the District of Columbia in 2026 (plus select local jurisdictions), subject to state-specific B2B/B2C exemptions and economic nexus thresholds.


A remittance document alone does not determine the result.


### Separate Card Settlement, Bank Transfers and FX


For the documented international-currency card flow, customer currency and settlement currency differ: settlements are made in INR irrespective of the payment currency. The[currency-conversion documentation](https://razorpay.com/docs/payments/international-payments/currency-conversion/?preferred-country=IN) describes conversion using the processing bank’s exchange rate on the payment date. Review the applicable fees and your actual settlement statement rather than assuming zero FX cost across products.


[International Bank Transfer](https://razorpay.com/docs/payments/international-payments/accept-international-payments-via-swift-transfer/?preferred-country=IN) has its own rails and settlement-account terms, including documented EEFC support. Confirm the chosen flow instead of applying a card rule to every international product.


### Confirm the Remittance Evidence Your Finance Team Needs


The[FIRS documentation](https://razorpay.com/docs/payments/dashboard/account-settings/firs/?preferred-country=IN) shows the dashboard listing monthly records in two sections: bank-provided certificates and Razorpay-generated statements. Keep that distinction visible with your AD bank. Indian export reporting also changed this year: the Export Declaration Form framework now covers service and software exports, as explained in the EDF filing guide for service exporters, and service export proceeds are ordinarily subject to a nine-month realisation period, or twelve months where exports are invoiced or settled in rupees. Practitioner analysis notes that a payment aggregator or an MoR changes who pays you and in what currency, not who files.


> **DID YOU KNOW:** The name of a remittance document does not tell you whether it meets a particular finance requirement. Check its issuer, the receipts it covers and how it reconciles to the relevant invoices.


## How Do You Calculate Whether Leaving an MoR Will Save Money?


Compare the actual MoR contract with the complete direct-selling stack over the same period and payment mix. Include processing, billing, FX, tax operations, refunds, disputes and migration. A lower processing rate justifies switching only when the resulting benefit remains positive after the services and risks your business takes back are included.


### Compare Equivalent Services Before Comparing Rates


Published standard MoR rates in 2026 commonly sit between roughly 3.9% plus 40 cents and 5% plus 50 cents before surcharges, but market ranges are not your contract. Use your own numbers.


Cost or operational item


MoR model


Direct-selling model


Transaction charges


Actual contracted bundle and fixed fees


Card or bank-transfer fees plus separately priced services


Billing and tax operations


Verify what the bundle covers


Required software, advisers, filings and staff time


FX and payout costs


Contracted conversion, transfer and payout terms


Product-specific conversion, transfer and settlement terms


Refunds and disputes

Migration

Integration, communications, authorisations and reconciliation


Do not add a gateway fee on top of an MoR price unless its contract charges one separately. Treat taxes collected for authorities separately from commercial fees, use consistent recoverable-tax assumptions across both models, and model payment success or churn only from your own comparable observations.


### Use a Break-Even Formula With Your Own Inputs


Monthly net benefit = V x (m – d) – O – K/H.


V is comparable monthly sales volume; m is the effective MoR variable cost rate; d is the effective direct variable cost rate; O is the incremental recurring operating cost of direct selling; K is one-time migration cost; H is the planning horizon in months. Include any differences in fixed MoR costs, and avoid counting a service in both d and O.


Break-even volume = (O + K/H) / (m – d), and only when m exceeds d. If it does not, the assumed fee spread cannot fund the added costs, so evaluate any non-fee benefit separately.


**Illustrative example, not provider pricing:** m = 6%; d = 3.5%; O = Rs 45,000 per month; K = Rs 1,20,000; H = 12 months. Break-even is Rs 22 lakh per month. At Rs 30 lakh per month, MoR cost is Rs 1,80,000 and direct cost is Rs 1,60,000 (including the monthly migration allocation), yielding a **net monthly saving of Rs 20,000** . At Rs 20 lakh per month, direct cost is Rs 1,25,000 against Rs 1,20,000 under an MoR, resulting in a **net monthly loss of Rs 5,000** .


> **PRO-TIP:** Recalculate with a smaller fee spread, a higher operating cost and a delayed migration. A decision that only works in the optimistic scenario needs more evidence.


## When Should an Indian SaaS Business Stay With an MoR?


Stay with an MoR when its contracted seller administration, supported buyer experience and operational support are worth more than the benefit of replacing them. A small finance team, complex market exposure, missing payment capabilities or risky subscriber migration can outweigh a lower direct-processing rate. Revisit the decision when those conditions change.


### Keep the MoR When Replacing Its Services Creates More Work Than Value


Stay if no one owns applicable tax assessment and filings, if your customer mix needs methods your approved direct setup does not support, if the contracted administration is genuinely valuable, or if the all-in direct cost fails the break-even test. The workload is also not static: the EU’s VAT in the Digital Age package rolls out progressively over the coming years. These are business-fit reasons, not evidence that a team is insufficiently mature.


### Use a Defined Split When Buyer Needs Differ


An Indian SaaS company might evaluate direct bank collections for an eligible enterprise segment while retaining an MoR for other sales. Define who invoices whom, the customer contract, tax treatment, renewal owner, and refund path for each segment. A split adds reconciliation work, so price that in. There is no percentage of international revenue at which a hybrid setup becomes mandatory.


## How Do You Move Away From an MoR Without Disrupting SaaS Renewals?


Treat an MoR exit as a change to contracts, billing, payment authorisations and financial operations. Approve the destination setup, inventory subscriptions and obligations, confirm portability, test lifecycle events, communicate with customers and migrate a controlled cohort. Retire old billing only after confirming the replacement schedule prevents both missed renewals and duplicate charges.


### Use an Eight-Step SaaS Migration Checklist


1. **Inventory what must move.** Export the permitted customer, subscription, plan, currency, renewal-date, invoice, credit, refund and entitlement records, then map each to an internal customer ID. Deliverable: an inventory with named owners and unresolved fields.
2. **Review the MoR exit agreement.** Confirm notice periods, termination rights, payout or reserve treatment, handling of historic refunds and disputes, data access and contractual changes. Establish which obligations stay with the old arrangement. Deliverable: a reviewed exit and run-off checklist.
3. **Approve and test the destination flows.** Confirm Razorpay account activation and the required cards, subscription features, or bank-transfer rails. Check the currencies and billing behaviours your customers actually use. Deliverable: an approved collection-flow matrix with gaps recorded.
4. **Confirm payment-method and authorisation portability.** Processor tokens generally stay inside the vault that issued them, and what may move is the underlying card data through a controlled process. Network tokens can sometimes survive a change, but typically only when the Token Requestor ID belongs to you rather than your provider, and provider-hosted subscription agreements may require a migration programme or buyer reauthorisation. Deliverable: a confirmed path per cohort, with no raw card details in spreadsheets.
5. **Prepare contracts, invoices and tax operations.** Assign the new seller relationship, customer notices, applicable registrations and filings, invoice requirements and export-record reconciliation. Review credits, tax-inclusive prices and service periods spanning the change. Deliverable: signed-off commercial and finance instructions.
6. **Test billing and access end-to-end.** Test a new signup, first authorisation, renewal, failed renewal, retry, plan change, cancellation, refund and entitlement update for every feature in use. Check webhook handling and reconciliation against internal records. Deliverable: observed test results plus a rollback procedure.
7. **Migrate a controlled cohort and reconcile every renewal.** Choose the cohort by risk and buyer workflow. Confirm the old and new billing schedules cannot double-charge or leave gaps. Explain any payment-detail action through your authorised customer communication process. Deliverable: cohort-level renewal and exception records.
8. **Expand only after acceptance criteria are met.** Check paid renewals, unintended churn, disputes, invoices, export records and support tickets. Complete run-off tasks and retain required history, remembering that international cardholders can raise disputes for up to 120 days while merchants typically have between 20 and 45 days to submit evidence, depending on the card network and the acquiring bank’s policies. Deliverable: a migration acceptance report naming unresolved liabilities and owners.


### Set Go-Live and Stop Criteria Before Moving the Next Cohort


Use your own current performance as the reference. Stop expansion if you see duplicate charges, unexplained entitlement loss, missing required authorisations, unresolved finance-record gaps or an unworkable customer recovery path. Investigate material renewal deterioration against a comparable cohort rather than applying a universal acceptable churn rate. A safe recovery may require fresh customer authorisation rather than an instant reversal to the old system, which is why the old arrangement usually stays open through run-off.


> **PRO-TIP:** Separate “new customers can pay” from “existing subscribers migrated successfully.” The first proves checkout works. The second requires verified renewal schedules, finance records and uninterrupted customer access.


## Frequently Asked Questions


### At What Revenue Should an Indian SaaS Business Leave an MoR?


There is no universal revenue threshold. Use your actual fee spread, incremental operating costs, migration cost and planning horizon to calculate break-even. Then check tax ownership, approved payment flows and renewal portability. Revenue can justify reviewing the model, but it cannot prove that direct collection is cheaper or operationally ready.


### Can an Indian SaaS Business Use Razorpay Instead of an MoR?


An eligible Indian SaaS business can evaluate Razorpay for direct international card collection, supported card subscriptions and invoice-led international bank transfers. Your company remains seller for those direct flows and arranges applicable tax and export operations. Confirm account activation, required features, currencies, commercial terms and migration feasibility first.


### Does Switching to Razorpay Remove Global Tax Responsibilities?


Direct collection does not transfer your seller tax responsibilities to the payment provider. Your business must arrange assessment and administration of the obligations that apply to its customers and markets. Tax software may support some tasks, while advisers and filings may still be needed. Review the actual transaction structure with Finance and Compliance before switching.


### Can Existing Subscriptions Move Without Asking Customers to Re-Enter Card Details?


Sometimes a supported secure transfer is possible, but do not assume it. Portability depends on both providers, the payment method, authorisations, contracts and the destination setup. Confirm the process before announcing a seamless migration. If fresh authorisation is needed, plan communication around renewal dates and verify that old and new schedules cannot double-charge.


### Can We Move Enterprise Invoices First and Keep Other Sales With an MoR?


A defined split can be appropriate when buyer needs differ and the contracts allow it. Evaluate an approved direct bank-transfer or card flow for the selected segment while keeping other sales under their existing arrangement. Document seller identity, invoicing, tax ownership, refunds and reconciliation for each route, and include the extra operating work in your cost comparison.
